$comment: The single written list of guards this project has earned. Read by scripts/guards.mjs, enforced by skills/doctrine/test/guard-parity.test.ts, rendered into GUARDS.md. `formats` names only the skills the defect is REACHABLE in: a static chart cannot have a stalled scroll step, and declaring it would be noise. `carried` means the skill's own verification script exports that decision function; `owed` is debt. `unreachable` is the third state and the one a reader needs prose for: a cell blank because it was MEASURED absent, or blank because the whole format works differently. Most blank cells need no entry — nobody would look for a scroll step in a static chart — so a reason is written exactly where one was retired after measurement, or where a format's whole column is blank and a reader would otherwise re-open the question.

guards.refuses: an asset inlined more than once into a self-contained delivered file
guards.earnedBy: a delivered route scrolly carried the same 340 KiB basemap plate five times — 1.33 MB of a 1.80 MB page, on a beat a newsroom would open on a phone

unreachable.dw-beat: the delivered web artefact is a page whose body is a single iframe to the hosted chart: it inlines no asset at all, so none can be inlined twice

guards.refuses: a raster plate and the overlay drawn on it fitting differently: cover pairs with slice, contain with meet, fill with none
guards.earnedBy: at 375x812 a plate cropped under an overlay that letterboxed drew Lisbon over Switzerland, at a scale that made every stop a 4px smear

unreachable.map-beat: retired after measurement, not left owed: object-fit appears in exactly two files in this tree, both scrolly IMAGE beats, and in no cartographic component. A map beat composites its plate as an <image> INSIDE the marks' own SVG, in their coordinate system, so there are not two projections that could disagree. The same defect is reachable here by the format's other mechanism, which is what plate-geometry-pairing was written for
unreachable.map-web: retired on the same measurement one task later: object-fit appears in none of the 23 web artifacts. This format composites its plate the way map-beat does, and pairs its ratio against the projected frame instead
unreachable.dw-beat: there is no raster plate and no overlay drawn on it: the artefact is one exported image, or an iframe to a hosted chart

guards.refuses: a baked plate whose aspect ratio is not the frame its own marks were projected into, so the default xMidYMid meet letterboxes it under them
guards.earnedBy: the same defect projection-pairing names, reached by this format's other mechanism: a map beat composites its plate as an <image> inside the marks' own SVG, where there is no object-fit to disagree with a preserveAspectRatio and the disagreement is between the plate's own ratio and its box

unreachable.dw-beat: nothing is baked here. There is no plate.png and no geometry.json recording the frame marks were projected into, because this format projects nothing

guards.refuses: a baked plate on the opposite luminance side from the ground its beat declares
guards.earnedBy: a beat declared ground #16191B and painted white labels on a dark halo over a dataviz-light plate: furniture correct for its theme, and unreadable
guards.alsoReachedBy: dw-beat, where the surface is not a baked plate but the PNG a delegated renderer hands back. This producer's spec requires an accent and has no field for a ground, so Datawrapper paints on whatever surface its own theme chooses and a story that declared a dark ground can be delivered a white rectangle. Same decision, same tuning constants, different measurement.

guards.refuses: a dash that measures its own path while vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke computes it in screen space, where that length does not live
guards.earnedBy: a river drawn as head, hole and tail because a pattern one route long was measured against a line the camera had scaled up 1.68x; six hours and five wrong diagnoses

unreachable.dw-beat: this producer authors no marks. A dashed rule is a Datawrapper enum (a range annotation's strokeType) drawn by Datawrapper's own renderer, and the vector-effect that makes the defect possible is not ours to write

guards.refuses: a mark still data-state=pending when the reveal has ended
guards.earnedBy: stop badges kept the fill they were SSR'd with while the line arrived at each of them: the narrative got there and the picture never said so

unreachable.dw-beat: there is no reveal: a delegated chart is one finished picture, and no mark is ever pending

guards.refuses: two consecutive steps painting the same picture
guards.earnedBy: a five-stop scrolly repainted 4.4 / 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0 % of its marks across four transitions: one identical picture, five times

unreachable.dw-beat: there are no steps: nothing here is driven by a reader's gesture or by a frame number

guards.refuses: a step whose picture never moves anywhere inside itself, on a beat built to scrub
guards.earnedBy: five finished SSR'd pictures passed every other guard and still jumped at each boundary: the line never drew under the reader's gesture

unreachable.dw-beat: there is nothing to scrub: a delegated chart has one state

guards.refuses: nothing on its own: it reads which of the two models a beat is built on, off the markup
guards.earnedBy: an assembly and a scrub owe different things, and guessing which is which misfires on both — the seed's four media have nothing to scrub between

unreachable.dw-beat: it reads which of the two scroll models a beat is built on, off the markup. A delegated chart is built on neither
